year.shelter: Nests of grass and moss in burrows under tree roots, stones and logs, and runs along hidden paths in the moss. In winter it lives in tunnels under the snow, where it's warmer.
year.young: Up to four litters a year from April to October, 3–6 young each; the first young can have their own young the same summer.

food.spring: Fresh green shoots, buds and leaves.
food.summer: Seeds, berries, mushrooms and green plants.
food.autumn: Seeds, berries and mushrooms; it stores seeds for winter.
food.winter: Seeds, roots and bark under the snow.

year.notes: The main food of foxes, kestrels, owls, weasels and many more. Vole numbers rise and crash every few years, and their hunters' young rise and fall with them.

text.title: Bank vole
text.stalk_hint: A vole! Get close quietly, then tap Pounce before it darts away.
text.about_looks: A small round rodent with a chestnut-red back, grey sides and a blunt nose. Its tail is about half as long as its body.
text.about_food: Seeds, berries, mushrooms and green plants. In winter, roots and bark under the snow.
text.about_home: Lives in the forest, nesting in burrows under tree roots and logs. It runs along hidden paths in the moss.
text.about_winter: Stays awake all winter in tunnels under the snow, where it's warmer than on top.
text.about_young: Up to four families a year, each of 3–6 young. Young born in spring can have their own young by summer.
text.about_fact: Foxes, kestrels and owls all live mostly on voles. When voles are many, those hunters raise more young.
text.dig: Digging... (a burrow keeps you safe and warm)
